surface.label: Antigravity workspace rules
surface.verified: Google Antigravity docs, "Rules" — .agents/rules/*.md, YAML frontmatter with trigger: always_on | model_decision | glob | manual; missing or invalid frontmatter silently discards the rule; trigger: glob takes comma-separated globs, which the docs require to be quoted so YAML does not read a leading * as an alias anchor; a 24 KB per-file limit and a 20,000-token budget for always_on rules, with automatic demotion to pointers past it
surface.note: This is why frontmatter is mandatory here and why the trigger value is not guessed: an unrecognised trigger means the rule is dropped with no message.

pointer.verified: Google Antigravity docs, "Rules": workspace rules are AGENTS.md or GEMINI.md in the root or any subdirectory; Copilot CLI also discovers GEMINI.md. Gemini CLI, read today: its own docs (core memory index, and the configuration reference) say the memory service loads GEMINI.md hierarchically from the working directory up to the project root and the home directory and also into subdirectories, and that `context.fileName` in settings.json "accepts either a single string or an array of strings" naming the context file(s) to load, default undefined
pointer.note: Covers Gemini CLI and gives Antigravity a second, equally-native name for the same file. A repository can also point Gemini CLI at AGENTS.md itself with `context.fileName: ["AGENTS.md"]` and need no pointer at all, which is the reason there is no separate Gemini CLI row here: this pointer and a native row would be two ways to hand one reader the same rule.

start.why: Antigravity rules docs: trigger is one of always_on, model_decision, glob, manual; model_decision injects only the path and description
Antigravity rules docs: AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md and .agents/AGENTS.md in the root or any subdirectory are always-on workspace rules, and they take no frontmatter
Antigravity rules docs: global modular rules at ~/.gemini/config/rules/*.md, alongside ~/.gemini/AGENTS.md and ~/.gemini/config/AGENTS.md

alsoReads.why: Antigravity rules docs: progressive disclosure — the path and description are injected and the body is opened on demand
Antigravity rules docs: .agents/rules/ is scanned flat — nested files are ignored unless registered in .agents/rules.json

loader.order: rules are cumulative across the global, workspace and directory scopes; directory scope is resolved by walking up from the edited file to the workspace root

cap.why: Antigravity rules docs: a rule file is truncated at 24,000 bytes, counted after @[label](path) includes are expanded

alsoCaps.why: Antigravity rules docs: past a 20,000-token budget the largest rules are demoted to a pointer line, "- <path>: <description>"

imports.why: Antigravity rules docs: @[label](path) inlines the file before the size limits are checked, with its frontmatter stripped; a bare @filename only rewrites to a canonical absolute path

loader.nested: cumulative — a rule applies to its directory and every subdirectory; the .agents/rules/ scan itself is flat
